section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the aims and hypotheses of the present study, which examined relationships between multidimensional interoceptive awareness (MAIA subscales) and multiple positive body-image constructs (body appreciation, body pride, functionality appreciation) as well as overweight preoccupation and appearance orientation. The authors state they recruited a large community sample of British women and men with a wide age range and planned to examine associations controlling for sex, age, and BMI. The section does not report sample size, demographic percentages, assessment instruments by name (for BA or BMI), survey method, or any correlation/statistical results.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: "The aim of the present study was to expand the available literature..."; "we sought to address these limitations in the present study by recruiting a large sample of British women and men, with a wide age range that would be more representative of age variations in community samples."; "we soughtto examine the extentto which dimensions of IA would be significantly associated outcome measures once sex, age, and BMI had been accounted for."
